nodes.name: game.py
nodes.summary: Core game engine for the Pacman AI projects: defines the Agent interface, direction constants, configurations, boolean grids, the game-state data packet, and the Game control loop that solicits actions from agents and applies rules.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `from util import *` star-imports, so utility helpers (TimeoutFunction, nearestPoint, raiseNotDefined) are resolved at module scope rather than through explicit imports.

nodes.name: Agent
nodes.summary: Abstract base class every Pacman agent extends; stores the agent index and declares getAction, which raises until a subclass overrides it.

nodes.name: Directions
nodes.summary: Namespace of movement constants (North, South, East, West, Stop) plus LEFT/RIGHT/REVERSE lookup tables used to rotate and invert directions.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Immutable-style (x, y) position plus travel direction with hashing and equality so configurations can key dictionaries, and generateSuccessor to translate along a movement vector.

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: Tracks one agent's configuration, pacman/ghost flag, scared timer and contest counters, with copy support for cloning game states.

nodes.name: Grid
nodes.summary: Boolean 2D grid backed by a list of lists, indexed grid[x][y], offering copy/count/asList queries and bit-packing helpers used to serialize food and wall maps compactly.

nodes.name: Actions
nodes.summary: Static helper collection that converts between direction names and movement vectors and enumerates legal moves and neighbors given a wall grid.

nodes.name: GameStateData
nodes.summary: Mutable data packet holding food, capsules, agent states, layout and score for a single game state, supporting deep copy, hashing and ASCII rendering of the board.

nodes.name: Game
nodes.summary: Central control loop: registers agents, enforces per-agent startup/move timeouts and exception catching, solicits actions, applies successors, updates the display and lets rules detect wins and losses.

nodes.name: reconstituteGrid
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a Grid from its packed (width, height, bits...) tuple representation and returns non-tuple input unchanged.

nodes.name: keyboardAgents.py
nodes.summary: Provides human-controlled Pacman agents that translate keyboard input (WASD/arrow keys, or IJKL for the second player) into legal movement actions.

nodes.name: KeyboardAgent
nodes.summary: Agent that reads waiting and pressed keys, maps them to a direction, then falls back to repeating the last legal move or a random legal action.

nodes.name: KeyboardAgent2
nodes.summary: Second keyboard-controlled agent using IJKL keys so two people can play interactively on one keyboard.

nodes.name: layout.py
nodes.summary: Loads and parses .lay maze files into Layout objects that expose walls, food, capsules and agent start positions, plus the lookup helpers the game and agents use to find layouts.

nodes.name: Layout
nodes.summary: Static description of a Pacman board: parses layout characters into wall and food grids, records capsule and agent positions, and offers corner, visibility and random-position helpers.

nodes.name: getLayout
nodes.summary: Locates and loads a named .lay layout file, searching the layouts directory and walking up parent directories when it is not found.

nodes.name: tryToLoad
nodes.summary: Attempts to open and parse a layout file, returning None when the path does not exist.

nodes.name: pacman.py
nodes.summary: Main entry point and rules layer for Pacman: defines the agent-facing GameState, the classic win/lose rules, pacman and ghost movement rules, and the CLI that wires layouts, agents and displays into games.
nodes.languageNotes: Agents are discovered dynamically at runtime by importing any *Agents.py module on PYTHONPATH and looking up the class by name, so agent files are not statically imported.

nodes.name: GameState
nodes.summary: Agent-facing view of the game: accessors for food, capsules, walls, pacman and ghost states and score, plus generateSuccessor which copies the state, applies an action and resolves collisions.

nodes.name: ClassicGameRules
nodes.summary: Classic Pacman rule set that creates games, detects wins and losses, reports progress and supplies the per-agent timeout budget.

nodes.name: PacmanRules
nodes.summary: Static rules for Pacman's movement: enumerate legal actions, apply an action to move pacman, and consume food or capsules with the resulting score changes.

nodes.name: GhostRules
nodes.summary: Static rules for ghost behavior: legal actions without stopping or reversing at intersections, movement with halved speed while scared, scared-timer decay and death collisions.

nodes.name: parseAgentArgs
nodes.summary: Parses comma-separated key=value agent arguments from the command line into a dict, treating bare keys as the value 1.

nodes.name: readCommand
nodes.summary: Builds the option parser, resolves the layout, instantiates the pacman and ghost agents, selects a display backend and returns the keyword arguments used to run games.

nodes.name: loadAgent
nodes.summary: Dynamically imports *Agents.py modules found on PYTHONPATH entries and returns the requested agent class by name.

nodes.name: replayGame
nodes.summary: Replays a recorded action list against a fresh game using a greedy pacman and random ghosts, updating the display frame by frame.

nodes.name: runGames
nodes.summary: Runs a batch of games with the given agents and display, optionally suppressing training games and recording histories, then prints aggregate scores and win rate.

nodes.name: pacmanAgents.py
nodes.summary: Baseline Pacman agents: a left-turning agent and a greedy agent that one-step-looks-ahead over legal actions using a pluggable evaluation function.

nodes.name: LeftTurnAgent
nodes.summary: Simple agent that prefers turning left, then continuing straight, then turning right, and reverses only as a last resort.

nodes.name: GreedyAgent
nodes.summary: One-ply greedy agent that scores every legal successor with an evaluation function resolved by name and randomly picks among the highest-scoring actions.

nodes.name: scoreEvaluation
nodes.summary: Default evaluation function returning the game state's current score.

nodes.name: ghostAgents.py
nodes.summary: Defines the ghost agent policies used during multi-agent search: an abstract GhostAgent plus uniformly random and Pacman-seeking/fleeing DirectionalGhost implementations that expose action probability distributions.

nodes.name: GhostAgent
nodes.summary: Abstract base ghost agent that samples an action from the distribution returned by getDistribution, falling back to STOP when no action is available.

nodes.name: RandomGhost
nodes.summary: Ghost policy that assigns equal probability to every legal action and returns the normalized uniform distribution.

nodes.name: DirectionalGhost
nodes.summary: Ghost policy that computes successor positions for each legal action and biases the distribution toward moves that minimize (attack) or maximize (scared flee) Manhattan distance to Pacman.

nodes.name: multiAgents.py
nodes.summary: Student implementation file for the adversarial search project, containing the reflex agent, the shared multi-agent search base class, and the Minimax, Alpha-Beta, and Expectimax agent skeletons plus evaluation functions.
nodes.languageNotes: Agent classes are selected at runtime by pacman.py via util.lookup, so class names must remain importable module-level symbols.

nodes.name: ReflexAgent
nodes.summary: Reflex agent that scores every legal action with an evaluation function and randomly picks among the highest-scoring moves; the evaluation function is the student-editable part.

nodes.name: scoreEvaluationFunction
nodes.summary: Default state evaluation function that simply returns the game score, intended for use by the adversarial search agents.

nodes.name: MultiAgentSearchAgent
nodes.summary: Abstract base for all adversarial search agents; stores Pacman's agent index, resolves the evaluation function by name through util.lookup, and parses the search depth.

nodes.name: MinimaxAgent
nodes.summary: Minimax search agent skeleton whose getAction is left unimplemented for the student to fill in, with docstring guidance on the GameState API.

nodes.name: AlphaBetaAgent
nodes.summary: Minimax-with-alpha-beta-pruning agent skeleton whose getAction must be implemented by the student.

nodes.name: ExpectimaxAgent
nodes.summary: Expectimax agent skeleton that models ghosts as choosing uniformly at random from their legal moves; getAction is left unimplemented.

nodes.name: betterEvaluationFunction
nodes.summary: Placeholder for the student's improved evaluation function (question 5), aliased as `better` at the bottom of the module.

nodes.name: util.py
nodes.summary: Shared utility module providing search data structures (Stack, Queue, PriorityQueue), the Counter distribution class, probability sampling helpers, dynamic name lookup, and timeout/print-suppression helpers used across the Pacman projects.
nodes.languageNotes: Counter subclasses dict with a default-zero __getitem__; note sortedKeys uses the Python 2 style `cmp=` argument to sort, a legacy artifact of the course codebase.

nodes.name: FixedRandom
nodes.summary: Wraps a random.Random instance seeded with a large hard-coded state blob so autograders and experiments can reproduce identical random sequences.
nodes.languageNotes: The bulk of the class is a 600-line literal tuple encoding Python's internal Mersenne Twister state.

nodes.name: Stack
nodes.summary: Minimal last-in-first-out container with push, pop, and isEmpty used by depth-first search agents.

nodes.name: Queue
nodes.summary: Minimal first-in-first-out container with push, pop, and isEmpty used by breadth-first search agents.

nodes.name: PriorityQueue
nodes.summary: Heap-backed priority queue that orders entries by priority with an insertion counter for tie-breaking and supports in-place priority updates.

nodes.name: PriorityQueueWithFunction
nodes.summary: PriorityQueue variant with Stack/Queue-compatible push signature, deriving each item's priority from a caller-supplied priority function.

nodes.name: manhattanDistance
nodes.summary: Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance between two 2D points, the standard heuristic in Pacman search and evaluation code.

nodes.name: Counter
nodes.summary: Dict subclass with default-zero lookups that models counts or probability distributions, with helpers for argmax, sorting, normalization, copying, and vector addition, subtraction, and dot product.

nodes.name: raiseNotDefined
nodes.summary: Reports the calling method, line, and file as unimplemented and exits, providing the standard marker for assignment stubs.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes either a Counter or a plain numeric vector so its values sum to one, returning the input unchanged when the total is zero.

nodes.name: nSample
nodes.summary: Draws n independent samples from a discrete distribution using the inverse-CDF method over sorted cumulative probabilities.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Samples a single value from a distribution given as either a Counter or a parallel list of values and probabilities.

nodes.name: sampleFromCounter
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that samples a key from a Counter by delegating to sample with the counter's sorted items.

nodes.name: getProbability
nodes.summary: Looks up the probability of a given value in a parallel values/probabilities distribution, returning zero when the value is absent.

nodes.name: flipCoin
nodes.summary: Returns True with probability p using random.random, a thin helper for Bernoulli trials.

nodes.name: chooseFromDistribution
nodes.summary: Samples one key from a Counter or (values, weights) pair after normalizing the weights, used by ghost agents to pick actions.

nodes.name: nearestPoint
nodes.summary: Rounds a continuous grid position to the nearest integer grid point.

nodes.name: sign
nodes.summary: Returns -1, 0, or 1 according to the sign of the given number.

nodes.name: arrayInvert
nodes.summary: Transposes a 2D array, swapping rows and columns.

nodes.name: matrixAsList
nodes.summary: Flattens a 2D matrix into a list of cells, optionally filtering to only those equal to a given value.

nodes.name: lookup
nodes.summary: Resolves a dotted name to a Python object, importing modules as needed, or searches a namespace for a uniquely matching symbol; raises on ambiguity or absence.

nodes.name: pause
nodes.summary: Prints a prompt and blocks until the user presses enter, used for step-by-step debugging of game runs.

nodes.name: TimeoutFunctionException
nodes.summary: Exception raised when a function wrapped by TimeoutFunction exceeds its allotted time.

nodes.name: TimeoutFunction
nodes.summary: Callable wrapper that enforces a time limit on a function using SIGALRM when available, otherwise measuring elapsed wall-clock time after the call.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on signal.alarm and is documented as non-reentrant; falls back to elapsed-time checking on platforms without SIGALRM.

nodes.name: mutePrint
nodes.summary: Redirects sys.stdout to a no-op writable object so agent debug prints are suppressed, remembering the original stream.

nodes.name: unmutePrint
nodes.summary: Restores the stdout stream saved by mutePrint, re-enabling console output.

nodes.name: VERSION
nodes.summary: One-line version stamp recording the CS188 project release number (v1.004) that this Pacman codebase corresponds to.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain-text single-token file with no parser support; it is read verbatim by release tooling rather than parsed as source code.

nodes.name: projectParams.py
nodes.summary: Project-wide configuration module that tells the autograder which student file to grade, which test-class module to load, the human-readable project name, and whether bonus questions are enabled.
nodes.languageNotes: A pure Python constants module: no imports, functions, or classes, only four uppercase module-level assignments that other modules read via attribute access.

layers.name: Game Engine & Rules
layers.description: The Pacman simulation core: the generic Game loop and Agent interface in game.py, plus pacman.py's GameState, win/lose and movement rules, and the command-line entry point that wires layouts, agents, and displays together.

layers.name: Shared Foundation
layers.description: Foundational support code every other module depends on: util.py's search data structures (Stack, Queue, PriorityQueue, Counter), probability and timeout helpers, and layout.py's .lay maze parsing and layout lookup.

layers.name: Adversarial Search Agents
layers.description: The student implementation surface for the multi-agent search assignment: ReflexAgent, the MultiAgentSearchAgent base class, and the Minimax, Alpha-Beta, and Expectimax agents with their evaluation functions in multiAgents.py.

layers.name: Agent Policies & Controls
layers.description: Alternative agent implementations loaded at runtime by name: baseline greedy and left-turning Pacman agents, the random and Pacman-seeking DirectionalGhost policies, and the keyboard-driven human agents.

layers.name: Project Metadata & Configuration
layers.description: Course-harness metadata rather than runtime logic: projectParams.py's autograder settings (student file, test class, bonus flags) and the VERSION release stamp for the CS188 project.
